sources.citation: WALS Online, language 'Vagla' (vag): 7 datapoints (imperatives from Crouch & Naden 1998; colour terms).
sources.note: No stress features (14A-17A) coded for Vagla.

sources.citation: Pike, Kenneth L. 1966. Tagmemic and matrix linguistics applied to selected African languages. Final report (OE contract). Ann Arbor: University of Michigan. ERIC ED010547.
sources.note: Vagala material (from Crouch) is clause/discourse syntax only. The only 'Stress is not phonemic.. borne by the syllable with the highest tone' passage (p.281) belongs to the Legbo phonological appendix, not Vagla.

sources.citation: Brindle, Jonathan. 2017. A dictionary and grammatical outline of Chakali. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: On Vagla only: 'Vagla, Dɛg, Tampulma, Sisaala, and Pasaale are all described with two tones (.. Crouch & Smiles 1966..)' (p.257). Nothing on Vagla stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2003. Plural verb morphology in Vagla. Gur Papers / Cahiers Voltaïques 6: 17-31.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2 'Vagla phonology' (pp.18-19): 24 consonants, 9-10 vowels with ATR harmony, all vowels long/short and nasalisable, 'Vagla has two level tones, rising, falling and downstep', tone-bearing final nasals/laterals. No stress/accent statement.

sources.citation: Hartell, Rhonda L. (ed.) 1993. Alphabets of Africa. Dakar: UNESCO-BREDA / SIL. p.167 'Vagala (Gur)'.
sources.note: Phoneme-grapheme table and alphabet only; silent on stress and tone.

sources.citation: Crouch, Marjorie. 1985. A note on syllable and tone in Vagla verbs. Journal of West African Languages 15(2): 29-40.
sources.note: Nothing. The paper treats syllable structure (CV, CVV, CVC, CVCV..) and tone only: 'The phonetic tones observed in isolated monosyllables are High, Low, Rise and Fall.. Downstepped High' (p.30); roots have underlying contrastive lexical tone; verb tone classes and sandhi. No mention of stress, accent or prominence anywhere in the 12 scanned pages (scanned read in full).

sources.citation: Bendor-Samuel, John T. 1965. The Grusi sub-group of the Gur languages. JWAL 2(1): 47-55.
sources.note: Lexicostatistical comparison including Vagala; nothing on stress.
